# dsh-desktop-quick-actions
Two round buttons at the foot of the DSH desktop sidebar:

- **Restart** — closes the app and starts it again, **without a console window ever appearing**.
- *
*Top up** — opens the DeepSeek top-up page in your system browser.

Windows only (the restart helper leans on WMI). The top-up button works anywhere the desktop
app run

ndows only (the restart helper leans on WMI). The top-up button works anywhere the desktop
app runs.
## Why another restart button

The obvious version of this plugin is four lines: `spawn('taskkill', ...)` then
`spawn(exe)`. It fai
ls in a way that is hard to guess from the code.

A console-subsystem child created through WMI gets a console of its own. On Windows 11 the
system ha

nds every new console to **Windows Terminal**, which is a separate process that
ignores `SW_HIDE` an
d `-WindowStyle Hidden`. So:

1. A black terminal window appears.
2. You close it, because why would you keep it.
3. Closing it se

nds `CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT` to everything attached to that console —
**including the app that was started

EVENT` to everything attached to that console —
**including the app that was started as its child**.

The app dies a few seconds after it came back. Nothing in the log says why, because nothing
crashed:
the window manager did exactly what it was told.

Measured on Windows 11 with DSH desktop 0.2.1-rc series. Before the fix: every
restart painted a `Wi

ndowsTerminal.exe` window. After: `Get-Process WindowsTerminal` returns
nothing, and the relaunch lo
g shows the whole path.
### What the fix does
Two layers, because one is not enough:
| Layer | Mechanism | Why |
| Launcher | `Invoke-CimMethod Win32_Process Create` → **`wscript.exe`** running a generated `.vbs`
with `WScript.Shell.Run cmd, 0, False` | `wscript.exe` is a GUI-subsystem program: it never allocate

s a console to begin with. No console, nothing for Terminal to take over. |
| App start | `Invoke-Ci
mMethod Win32_Process Create` for the app itself | The new process is owned by `WmiPrvSE.exe` and in
herits no console, so no later window closing can reach it. |
`Start-Process` remains as a fallback if WMI is unavailable.
## The port is read, never assumed

The desktop host binds a **fresh port on every launch**. A hardcoded port number is wrong by
the sec

ond restart. The host half reads `req.headers.host` — the request that triggered the
restart already

knows the port — and passes it to the helper as `-Port`. When it cannot be
determined, the helper s
kips the port checks and waits on the process instead.
## Install

Restart the app once by hand. After that, the button works.
## Routes
| Method | Path | Purpose |
| `GET` | `/dsh-quick-actions/info` | Diagnostics: app pid, exe path, helper present, top-up URL, de

tected port, platform |
| `POST` | `/dsh-quick-actions/restart` | Start the detached helper |
| `POS

T` | `/dsh-quick-actions/open` | Open an `https://` URL in the default browser |
| `POST` | `/dsh-qu
ick-actions/rendered` | Client reports where it painted (layout probe) |
`/open` accepts **only `https://`** — no `file:`, no `javascript:`, no bare paths.
## Safety

- The helper reads the target pid's `ExecutablePath` first and **aborts** if it does not match
the e

xecutable it is about to start. It never kills a process that merely inherited the pid.
- The origin

al command line is preserved, so custom flags such as `--user-data-dir` survive a restart.
- `NODE_O

PTIONS` is stripped from the child environment so the relaunched app does not inherit
an injected lo

ader.
- Every step appends to `~/.dsh/desktop-quick-actions.log`. If a restart fails, that file says
which step refused and why.

## Compatibility

- DSH desktop `0.2.1-rc.*` and later. Needs the `webServer` service, which the desktop host
provides

; in a plain `dsh web` profile the routes are skipped and the plugin logs why.
- Windows 10/11 for t

he restart half. Node 20+.
- Nothing throws at import time — a failed loader entry makes the desktop

app show its
recovery dialog, so every step is guarded and logged.
